items.text: Hey, good to see you again. Come on in.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Thanks, Doc. Appreciate you squeezing me in today.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Of course. How was the drive over?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Not bad. Traffic on the 405 was about what you'd expect.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Yeah, it always is at this hour. Alright, let me pull up your chart here.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Take your time.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Okay. So what brings you in today? What's the main thing on your mind?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Well, two things really. My right shoulder's been bothering me for about three weeks now.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: And I wanted to check in with you about my sugars. I don't think they've been great.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Okay, so right shoulder pain and diabetes follow-up. Got it.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: And honestly, I've been feeling pretty down lately too. I wasn't sure if I should mention it.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: I'm really glad you did mention it. We'll talk through all three.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Alright.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Let's start with the shoulder. When did the pain start exactly?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: About three weeks ago. I was helping my son move a sofa up the stairs and felt a twinge.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: A twinge when you were lifting?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Yeah, right when we were lifting it up over the landing. Sharp at first, then it settled into an ache.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Where exactly does it hurt? Can you point to it?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Right here, on the top, kind of going down into my upper arm.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Does it hurt more with certain movements?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Reaching overhead is the worst. I can't put a shirt on without wincing.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: What about at night? Does it wake you up?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Yeah, if I roll onto that side. I've been sleeping on my left to avoid it.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Any numbness or tingling going down the arm?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: No, no numbness, no tingling.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Any weakness? Trouble gripping things, opening jars?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Grip feels fine. It's just the pain that limits me.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Have you tried anything for it?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Ice, Tylenol, some of that muscle rub. None of it did much.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Mm-hmm.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: I took two ibuprofen a couple times which helped for a few hours but I didn't want to keep doing that with my stomach.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Okay. Let's talk about the sugars. Are you checking at home?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Yeah, morning and before dinner, most days.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: And what are you seeing?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Mornings, they've been running one-sixty to one-eighty. Before dinner, one-forty or so, sometimes higher.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Those are higher than where we want them. Any changes to your diet or activity?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Honestly, the holidays kind of got me. More bread, more dessert than I should have. And I haven't been walking as much since it got cold.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Got it. Any symptoms? Increased thirst, getting up at night to pee more than usual?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: I do get up once or twice a night, but that's been the same for years.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: No blurred vision, no tingling in your feet, nothing new?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: No. Feet feel normal.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: And the mood thing. Tell me more about that.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Just, I don't know. Low energy. I haven't been enjoying things the way I used to.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: How long has that been going on?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Maybe two months? Since my brother passed.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: I'm really sorry.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Thanks. It's just hit me harder than I thought it would.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Any trouble sleeping? Appetite changes?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: I'm sleeping more than usual, honestly. And not eating as much.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Any thoughts of hurting yourself?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: No, nothing like that. I just feel kind of empty.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Let me just run through a few review questions. Any chest pain or shortness of breath with exertion?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: No chest pain. I do get winded on the stairs but I blame that on being out of shape.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Any palpitations, racing heart?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: No.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Any cough, wheezing, trouble breathing?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: No.
items.speaker: UNSPECIFIED

items.text: Any belly pain, nausea, changes in bowel habits?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Actually, my stomach's been acting up again. Heartburn, especially at night.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Are you taking your omeprazole daily?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Most days. I forget on weekends sometimes.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Any blood in the stool, black stools?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: No, nothing like that.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Any urinary issues, burning, frequency?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: No.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Fevers, chills, night sweats?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: None of that.
items.speaker: UNSPECIFIED

items.text: Any rashes or skin issues?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Nope.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Any headaches, dizziness, vision changes?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: No headaches. Vision's fine.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Let me go through your history to make sure I've got everything current. You've got type 2 diabetes, that's been, what, fifteen years now?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Right, diagnosed in 2010.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: High blood pressure, diagnosed about ten years ago.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Yeah, around 2015.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: High cholesterol, and GERD. Anything else I'm missing?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: No, I think that's the list.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: No history of heart disease, no stroke, no cancer.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Right.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Surgical history. You had your gallbladder out in 2010, right?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Yeah, laparoscopic. Outpatient.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: And appendix as a kid.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Age ten or so.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Any other surgeries? Hernia, anything like that?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: No, that's it.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Family history. Your mom had heart disease, is that right?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Yeah, she had a heart attack at sixty-two. Passed at seventy-eight from a second one.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: And your dad had diabetes.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Type 2 diabetes, yeah. He's still alive, in his nineties, actually.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Any cancer in the family?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: My aunt had breast cancer. Nothing in my immediate family.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Siblings healthy?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: My brother — the one who passed — he had heart disease too. That's part of why I'm a little worried.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Social history. You quit smoking about ten years ago, forty pack-year history before that.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Right. Haven't touched a cigarette since 2015.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: So for the chart, that puts you down as a former smoker rather than a current one. Nothing at all since then, no cigars, no chewing tobacco, no vaping?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Nothing at all. No cigars, no chew, no vape pens. I quit cold turkey in 2015 with the patch and I haven't gone back once.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: That's a real accomplishment. I'm going to note the forty pack-year history along with the 2015 quit date, because that exposure still matters for your lung and heart risk.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Understood. My wife made me throw the last pack out the window, honestly.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Good. Alcohol?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Two beers a week, usually on Fridays.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Let me put a frequency on that. How often would you say you have a drink containing alcohol? Two to four times a month, or more like two to three times a week?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Two to four times a month. It's really just the Friday beers, so four times a month at the very most.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: And on a day when you do drink, how many drinks are we talking about?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Two. Two or fewer, every single time. I don't finish a third.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Over the past year, has there been any occasion where you had six or more drinks at one sitting?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: No, never. Not one time in the past year, and honestly not in twenty-some years.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Good, so nothing heavier than that pattern anywhere in the last twelve months.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Two beers on a Friday night is the whole story.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Any recreational drugs?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: No, never.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: No marijuana, no edibles or gummies? And nobody else's prescription pills?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: None of that. No marijuana, no edibles, and I've never taken a pill that wasn't mine.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Any caffeine or energy drinks worth noting?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Two cups of coffee in the morning and that's it. No energy drinks, no soda.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: I'll write that down as no recreational substance use, caffeine limited to two cups of coffee a day.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: You're retired now, is that right? You were an electrician.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Thirty-five years as a union electrician. Retired three years ago.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: And you live with your wife.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Married forty-two years this June.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Congratulations. Any exercise? You mentioned the walking.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: I was walking a mile or two most days. It's dropped off since the weather turned.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Let's put some numbers on the exercise. Would you say you're exercising on a regular basis right now, yes or no?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Yes, I'd still call it regular. Not as much as I was in the fall, but I'm still getting out there on a schedule.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: In an average week, how many days do you actually exercise?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Three days a week right now. It was five or six before it got cold.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: And on the days when you do exercise, how long are you going for?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Between twenty and forty minutes. Call it half an hour most times, door to door.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: What type of exercise is it? Just the walking, or anything else?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Mostly brisk walking around the neighborhood with my wife. I also do about ten minutes of light stretching for my back a couple of mornings a week.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: So brisk walking three days a week, twenty to forty minutes, plus some light stretching. That's a solid base to build back from.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: The goal is getting back to daily walks once it warms up a little.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Let's go through your meds. You're on metformin one thousand milligrams twice daily.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Right, one in the morning, one at dinner.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Lisinopril twenty milligrams once a day.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Yep, every morning.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Atorvastatin forty milligrams at bedtime.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Yep.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: And omeprazole twenty milligrams daily.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Right. Though like I said, I miss a dose sometimes on weekends.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Anything else you're taking that's not on the list? Supplements, vitamins, anything over the counter?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Oh, yeah. I started taking turmeric. My neighbor swears by it for joint pain.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: How much are you taking?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: One capsule in the morning, five hundred milligrams I think.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Okay, I'll add that to your list. Any aspirin?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: No. You told me to stop it a while back.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Allergies. You've got penicillin on the list, reaction is hives.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Right. Happened when I was in my twenties. Broke out in hives all over.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Any trouble breathing, swelling of the face?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: No, just the hives. I'd call it moderate, I guess.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Any other drug allergies?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: No. Just penicillin.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Food allergies, environmental?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: No, I'm good there.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Immunizations. You got your flu shot in October, I see.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Right, at the pharmacy.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: You're up to date on pneumonia. And you got your COVID booster last fall.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Yeah, I got the updated one.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Shingrix — you completed the series a couple years back.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Yep.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Good. You're caught up.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Let me go over your vitals from today. Blood pressure is 146 over 88.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: That's higher than usual.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: It is. Pulse is 74, respirations 16. Oxygen saturation 97 percent on room air.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Okay.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Temperature 98.2. Weight 198 pounds. And height is 5 feet 10 inches.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: I've gained a few pounds over the holidays.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Your BMI puts you in the overweight range. We'll talk about that with the diabetes.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Alright, let me take a look at you. Deep breath in. And out.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Okay.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: General appearance. You're alert and oriented, comfortable, in no acute distress. You do look a little tired today, though.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: I haven't had much energy lately.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Lungs are clear bilaterally, no wheezing or crackles.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Mm-hmm.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Heart — regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs, no gallops. Carotids without bruits.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Good.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: HEENT exam unremarkable — ears, nose, throat all normal. Neck supple, no thyromegaly, no lymphadenopathy.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Okay.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Abdomen is soft, bowel sounds are normal, no masses. There is some mild tenderness right up here in the epigastrium when I press.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Yeah, that's the spot that burns at night.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Let me check your feet — diabetic foot exam. Dorsalis pedis pulses 2 plus bilaterally. Monofilament intact. No ulcers.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Good, good.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Extremities. I'm seeing trace edema at both ankles. I want that documented before we start the amlodipine, because ankle swelling is the side effect we watch for.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: My socks do leave a mark by the end of the day.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Skin is warm and dry, no rashes anywhere. There's a callus on the ball of your right foot, no breakdown around it.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: I've had that callus for years.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Now let me look at that shoulder. Raise your arm up. Good, stop there.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Yeah, that's where it hurts.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Pain with abduction past 90 degrees. Positive Neer's impingement sign. Negative Hawkins. No weakness with resisted external rotation. Sensation intact.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Alright.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Consistent with rotator cuff tendinitis or impingement.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Neuro. Cranial nerves are intact, strength is five out of five in all four extremities, and your gait is steady.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Okay.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: One more thing for the exam. Your affect is flat today and you're making less eye contact than usual. Speech is normal, thought process is linear.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: I've noticed that myself, honestly.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Let me pull up your labs from last week. Your hemoglobin A1C came back at 7.8.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: That's worse than last time.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: It is. Last visit it was 7.1. So it's drifted up. LDL cholesterol is 142.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: That's high too.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: HDL 38, also low. Triglycerides 210. Creatinine 1.1, eGFR 68 — kidney function stable. Liver panel normal, TSH normal.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Okay.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: So the metabolic numbers are the things we need to work on.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Alright. Let me go through my assessment and plan. Problem one — type 2 diabetes, uncontrolled.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Yep.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Your A1C's drifted up from 7.1 to 7.8. I want you to continue your metformin at 1000 milligrams twice daily as prescribed.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Okay.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Let's really focus on getting back to walking daily and cutting the sweets back. We'll repeat the A1C in three months and reassess then.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Alright, I can do that.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Problem two — hypertension, uncontrolled.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: My pressure's up.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Today you're 146 over 88, that's too high. You're already on lisinopril twenty milligrams. I'd like to add amlodipine 5 milligrams once daily to get you to goal.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Amlodipine.
items.speaker: UNSPECIFIED

items.text: Right. Side effect to watch for is ankle swelling. If that happens, let me know. We'll recheck your pressure in four weeks.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Okay.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Problem three — hyperlipidemia. LDL is 142, which is higher than I'd like.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: I thought the statin was working.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: It is helping. For now let's continue your atorvastatin 40 milligrams at bedtime and focus on diet and exercise. We'll recheck lipids in three months.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Got it.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Problem four — right rotator cuff tendinitis, new diagnosis.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: That's the shoulder.
items.speaker: UNSPECIFIED

items.text: Right. I'm going to refer you to orthopedics for further evaluation. They may want imaging to rule out a tear. In the meantime, rest the arm, ice it, and you can keep using Tylenol as needed.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Okay.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: If the pain doesn't improve in two weeks, we'll look at further options.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Problem five — GERD, stable on omeprazole.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Mostly stable.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Continue omeprazole 20 milligrams daily, and really try to take it every day, including weekends.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Alright.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Problem six — major depressive disorder, new.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Yeah.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Your PHQ-9 today was 12, that's moderate depression. Given the context of your brother's passing, some of this is grief. I'd like to hold off on medication for now and have you see a therapist. I'll give you some names on the way out.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Okay.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Any thoughts of hurting yourself, you call me immediately. And I want to see you back in two weeks for a mood check.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: I will.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Let me jot down some follow-up items. Add a task to call the patient on Friday with the repeat lab results once they're back.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Friday, okay.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Add a task for the MA to schedule the orthopedics referral within 48 hours — we don't want that shoulder waiting.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Good.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: And add a task to check in with the patient in one week about their mood to make sure they're doing okay.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Sounds good.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Any questions for me before we wrap up?
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Just — how soon before the new blood pressure med kicks in?
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: The amlodipine, within a couple weeks you should see your numbers come down.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Alright.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: I'll see you back in two weeks for the mood check and four weeks for the blood pressure check. Call the office if anything comes up before then.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: Will do. Thanks, Doc.
items.speaker: PATIENT

items.text: Take care now.
items.speaker: DOCTOR

items.text: You too.
items.speaker: PATIENT
